subject: Post-call: MeridianOne inference fit & topology recap

Subject: Post-call: MeridianOne inference fit & topology recap

Ariel / Priya — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared record.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: unpredictable latency during peak batch processing (customer search + summarization flow) and rising per-token costs when traffic spikes.
- Goal: 95th percentile end-to-end generation latency < 250ms for short summarization requests (~256 tokens) and steady throughput ~120 req/s with 3x burst headroom.
- Deployment preference: private VPC control plane (data residency + KMS) with a Dedicated pool for steady traffic, plus hosted fallback variants for burst smoothing.

What we discussed (high level)
- Workload: mixed chat + extractive summarization. 60% of calls are short completions (<= 256 tokens), 30% mid (256–1024), 10% long ( >1024).
- SLO targets: 95th <= 250ms for short, p50 <= 90ms; tail latency for long requests acceptable to be higher but want consistent retries/fallbacks.
- Cost sensitivity: target amortized cost per short completion <$0.008 (model + infra).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 reports required for procurement; must support customer-managed KMS and VPC peering.

Initial technical observations / constraints
- We expect the model candidate to be ~7B–13B parameter family, running int8 quantized. KV cache for session state is important for chat use-cases — prefix caching will reduce token work for repeated contexts.
- Autoscaling needs fast cold-start mitigation: recommend a small warm pool and burst capacity policy (Dedicated reserved + hosted fallback).
- Network egress: routing through their private peering (we documented peering requirements during call).

Action items (owner, ETA)
1) Jordan: send this recap + stats template and attach our topology draft — attached. (today)
2) MeridianOne: fill in the traffic profile CSV I attached (sample rows in meridianone-inference-stats.csv) and confirm peak qps and percentiles. (by Wed 07/31)
3) Karthik: produce a short topology/options note (Dedicated sizing + fallback variants) and recommended autoscale thresholds. (Mon 07/31)
4) Schedule technical deep dive (model selection + latency tuning) — suggested Wed Aug 2, 14:00 PT. Please confirm.

Questions we still have from our side
- Can you confirm whether PII is present in requests? If yes, what masking/encryption workflows are required?
- Any hard constraints on model family (e.g., strict requirement to run open-source weights vs approved vendor models)?

Attachments
- meridianone-inference-stats.csv (sample traffic profile)
- redwood-deploy-topology-draft.pdf (draft suggested topology for Dedicated + fallback)

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick call if anything above needs correction.

Best,
Jordan Blake

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. Looks good to us; a couple quick notes: 

1) We'll populate the CSV by EOD Wednesday — current average qps is ~40 during business hours with 3 major spikes per day hitting ~150 qps sustained for 4–6 minutes.
2) PII: yes — request payloads can contain customer PII (names, emails, small snippets). We need at-rest encryption and customer-managed keys.
3) Model family: we prefer running open weights in our Dedicated pool due to licensing, but are open to Redwood-managed hosted fallbacks for bursts if you can guarantee similar latency behavior and consistent outputs.

Two clarifying questions from our engineering lead (cc'd Priya):
- What cold-start time do you typically see for new Dedicated workers at scale (we're most concerned about the 3–6 minute spikes)?
- Can you sketch how fallback routing would preserve session-level KV state for consistency across model variants?

Happy to confirm Wed Aug 2 at 14:00 PT once you share the topology note.

Subject: Re: Post-call: MeridianOne inference fit & topology recap (tech note)

Jordan / Grace — quick tech note to add ahead of the deep dive. Attaching a short PDF (redwood-deploy-topology-draft.pdf) with concrete sizing options. Highlights: 

- Dedicated sizing: for steady 120 req/s with 3x burst headroom, recommend starting with 8 x A10G-equivalent instances (sharded runtime) with an autoscale policy to +50% on CPU/GPU queue latency signals. That gives warm capacity to absorb typical bursts.
- Cold-start: warm start time for a preloaded quantized 7B model is ~12–18s per worker if KV is pre-warmed; full cold start (binary + weight load) can be 90–120s depending on instance type. Hence the warm pool recommendation.
- Fallback routing: implement prefix/KV cache replication to a shared Redis cluster (encrypted in transit & at rest) accessible to both Dedicated and hosted variants. On fallback, we proxy metadata so session identity maps to the same KV keys — outputs won't be byte-for-byte identical across different model variants but we can preserve context and reduce recompute.
- Batching: dynamic batching across similar latency windows, target batch sizes 8–16 for short completions. Add per-route QoS to prioritize low-latency calls.

I'll bring the topology slides to the Aug 2 deep dive and we can iterate with MeridianOne infra.

Karthik
